new_libraries.name: ESP32KeyBridge
new_libraries.author: TANAKA Masayuki
new_libraries.sentence: Bridge keyboard input to keyboard output on ESP32: remap, layers, macros, and layout conversion in between.
new_libraries.paragraph: ESP32KeyBridge sits between a keyboard and the machine that reads it. It takes input from USB Host keyboards, mice, gamepads and MIDI devices, BLE HID keyboards and mice, GPIO switches, key matrices and rotary encoders, normalizes it into one key model, merges several inputs into one, applies single-step remapping across key kinds, momentary layers, disabled keys, text macros and keyboard layout conversion, and writes the result to USB Device HID, BLE HID, or a serial Print. The core is portable C++ with no Arduino, ESP-IDF or hardware dependency; adapters are header-only, so a sketch needs EspUsbHost, EspUsbDevice or EspBle only for the adapters it includes.
